description: The TypeScript kit parser's reading of spec/ir/mck, per case file. A Rust parser test compares itself with this for every file whose sha256 still matches.

cases.title: Access-controlled definition, three spellings
prose: Closed by bead morphir-j442: the flattened form validates beside the tag form and the legacy form. The tag form is canonical.

cases.title: Opaque type specification is an empty object
Custom type definition with constructors
prose: Decision 0007 names a constructor's slots parameters in the model; the wire spelling, a list of `[name, type]` pairs per constructor, is unchanged.

fences.body:
CustomTypeDefinition:
  typeParams: [a]
  access: Public
  constructors:
    just: [[value, a]]
    nothing: []

inputs:
  a: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  b: morphir/SDK:basics#int
output: morphir/SDK:basics#int

ExpressionBody:
  inputTypes:
    x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  body:
    Variable: x

cases.title: Documentation on a definition
prose: Decision 0010: `doc` is a flattened member placed first beside the variant. The nested `{ "doc", "value" }` wrapper is accepted for the window of decision 0006. Bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.5.

fences.body:
Public:
  doc: The user's display name
  TypeAliasDefinition:
    typeParams: []
    typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string

cases.title: Native and external bodies
prose: Decision 0008: `ExternalBody` carries a list of per-target bindings and an optional fallback `body`, so a Gleam-style external with a body encodes faithfully. The single-binding spelling with `externalName` and `targetPlatform` at the top level is accepted for the window of decision 0006 as a one-entry list.

fences.body:
ExternalBody:
  inputTypes:
    msg: morphir/SDK:string#string
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#unit
  externals:
    - targetPlatform: javascript
      externalName: console.log

cases.title: External body with two bindings and a fallback
prose: Decision 0008: targetPlatform values are unique within externals.

fences.body:
ExternalBody:
  inputTypes:
    x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  externals:
    - targetPlatform: erlang
      externalName: math:abs
    - targetPlatform: javascript
      externalName: Math.abs
  body:
    Variable: x

NativeBody:
  inputTypes:
    a: morphir/SDK:basics#int
    b: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  nativeInfo:
    hint:
      Arithmetic: {}

cases.title: Documentation on a value specification
prose: Decision 0010: a value specification's `doc` is first beside its own members; the nested `{ "doc", "value" }` wrapper is accepted for the window.

fences.body:
types: {}
values:
  add:
    doc: Adds two integers
    inputs:
      a: morphir/SDK:basics#int
      b: morphir/SDK:basics#int
    output: morphir/SDK:basics#int

cases.title: Type alias specification
prose: A specification states a type's shape without an access level; `typeParams` comes before `typeExp`, as it does in the matching definition (definitions-0001).

cases.title: Custom type specification
prose: The constructor map is the same `[name, type]` pair list the definition uses (definitions-0003); a specification has no `access` member, because the whole specification is the public face of the type.

fences.body:
CustomTypeSpecification:
  typeParams: [a]
  constructors:
    just: [[value, a]]
    nothing: []

cases.title: Derived type specification
prose: A derived type names the type it is built from and the two functions that convert between them. All four members are required, and the two conversions are FQNames, not expressions.

fences.body:
DerivedTypeSpecification:
  typeParams: []
  baseType: morphir/SDK:string#string
  fromBaseType: my-org/project:module#from-string
  toBaseType: my-org/project:module#to-string

cases.title: Incomplete type definition, a hole with a type mismatch
prose: Decision 0008 puts `Hole` in the value expressions; the v4 schema's `IncompleteTypeDefinitionBody` puts type-level incompleteness in a definition rather than in a type expression (types-0011). An `IncompleteTypeDefinition` carries its `typeParams`, an `incompleteness`, and an optional `partialTypeExp` — what the author had written when the definition stopped being complete. A `Hole`'s `reason` says why; `TypeMismatch` names the expected and the found type as strings.

fences.body:
IncompleteTypeDefinition:
  typeParams: [a]
  incompleteness:
    Hole:
      reason:
        TypeMismatch:
          expected: morphir/SDK:basics#int
          found: morphir/SDK:string#string

cases.title: Draft type definition with a partial type expression
prose: `Draft` is the second incompleteness: the definition is deliberately unfinished rather than broken, so it takes an empty payload and no reason. The `partialTypeExp` it keeps is an ordinary type expression.

fences.body:
IncompleteTypeDefinition:
  typeParams: []
  incompleteness:
    Draft: {}
  partialTypeExp: morphir/SDK:basics#int

cases.title: Incomplete value definition
prose: Decision 0008 consequence 2: a hole inside a body and an incomplete body are different things. An `IncompleteBody` is the fourth value definition body; its `outputType` is optional, because an incomplete definition may not have one yet, and its `incompleteness` uses the same vocabulary the type side does. `DeletedDuringRefactor` spells its transaction identifier `tx-id` on the wire.

fences.body:
IncompleteBody:
  inputTypes:
    x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  incompleteness:
    Hole:
      reason:
        DeletedDuringRefactor:
          tx-id: tx-42

cases.title: Private access-controlled definition
prose: `Private` is the other access level of definitions-0001 and takes the same three spellings. Decision 0010: the nested `{ "doc", "value" }` wrapper is accepted for the window of decision 0006 under `Private` exactly as it is under `Public` (definitions-0006). The fence below carries no `doc`, so it shows only the unwrapping half: the payload under `value` moves up beside the access tag.

cases.title: Access-controlled value definition, public
prose: The value twin of definitions-0001 and definitions-0006. `readAccessControlled` is shared with the type side, so the same three access spellings and the same documentation rules apply; the node kind is its own, so the kit states it in its own case. Decision 0010: `doc` is flattened beside the variant, and the nested `{ "doc", "value" }` wrapper is accepted for the window of decision 0006.
The fence below is the nested wrapper: the definition sits under `value` instead of beside `doc`. A reader normalizes it to the canonical fence above and reports `legacy_spelling`.

fences.body:
Public:
  doc: Adds two integers
  ExpressionBody:
    inputTypes:
      a: morphir/SDK:basics#int
      b: morphir/SDK:basics#int
    outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
    body:
      Variable: a

cases.title: Private access-controlled value definition
prose: `Private` on the value side, the twin of definitions-0017. The nested `{ "value" }` wrapper is accepted for the window of decision 0006 under `Private` exactly as it is under `Public` (definitions-0018); the fence below carries no `doc`, so it shows only the unwrapping half.

fences.body:
Private:
  ExpressionBody:
    inputTypes: {}
    outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
    body:
      Variable: x

cases.title: Annotations on a type specification
prose: A specification may carry `annotations`, written first and only when non-empty. Each is either the compact string `pkg:mod#local` or `pkg:mod#local:free text` (the separator is the first colon after `#`), or the structured object `{ "name", "arguments" }` whose arguments are positional values or named `{ "name", "value" }` pairs. `arguments` is omitted when empty. Definitions never carry annotations (definitions-0023).

fences.body:
TypeAliasSpecification:
  annotations:
    - my-org/project:annotations#deprecated:Use user-v2 instead
    - name: my-org/project:annotations#since
      arguments:
        - Literal:
            StringLiteral: 1.2.0
        - name: reason
          value:
            Literal:
              StringLiteral: renamed
    - name: my-org/project:annotations#internal
  typeParams: []
  typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string

annotations: ["my-org/project:annotations#pure"]
inputs:
  x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
output: morphir/SDK:basics#int

cases.title: Annotations on a module specification
prose: `annotations` comes first; `doc` stays last (decision 0010).

cases.title: A definition carries no annotations
prose: Annotations belong to specifications, the public face; inside a definition the member is unknown.

cases.title: A hole incompleteness keeps a partial body
prose: A `Hole` says why under `reason` and may keep what the author had as `partialBody`, a type expression; the member is written only when present (definitions-0014 has none).

fences.body:
IncompleteTypeDefinition:
  typeParams: []
  incompleteness:
    Hole:
      reason:
        UnresolvedReference:
          target: my-org/project:module#missing
      partialBody: morphir/SDK:basics#int

cases.title: An incomplete body keeps a partial value
prose: The value twin of definitions-0024: `partialBody` on an `IncompleteBody` is a value expression, written after `incompleteness` and only when present.

fences.body:
IncompleteBody:
  inputTypes: {}
  outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
  incompleteness:
    Draft: {}
  partialBody:
    Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 1

cases.title: Draft is an incompleteness, not a hole reason
prose: A hole's reason is `UnresolvedReference`, `DeletedDuringRefactor` or `TypeMismatch` (definitions-0014, 0016). `Draft` is the other incompleteness kind (definitions-0015) and names no reason; a reason must be a wrapper object.

cases.title: An input type is a bare type
prose: Each entry of `inputTypes` is a type expression and nothing else; there is no per-parameter attributes member.

cases.title: Documentation is one string
prose: `doc` is a string wherever a node carries it (decision 0010). An array of lines is accepted only in a module manifest file (document-tree page), never here.

cases.title: A value specification without inputs writes none
prose: `inputs` is omitted when empty and accepted when written empty.

cases.title: A platform-specific native hint names its platform
prose: `PlatformSpecific` requires `platform`; a reader does not invent one.

cases.title: priv is not an access spelling
prose: The access spellings are `Public`, `public`, `pub`, `Private` and `private` (definitions-0001, 0017). `priv` is none of them.

cases.title: Format version spellings
prose: Governed by `docs/spec/ir/format-version.md` and its corpus. Integer 4 is canonical for 4.0.0; a later minor is not supported.

cases.title: A v3 tagged-array distribution is not a v4 document
prose: `tests/bdd/fixtures/ir/v4/v4-library-distribution.json` carried this shape. Bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.11.

cases.title: Complete library, JSON and YAML agree
prose: The published complete example and its YAML rendering are the same distribution. Both write record fields under `fields` (decision 0004), the SDK as `morphir/SDK` (decision 0011), and the list function's `parameterType` (decision 0007).

`website/static/ir/examples/v4/complete-example.json` is the human-readable form the docs site publishes: it is pretty-printed and spells its format version `"4.0.0"`, both of which a reader accepts and a writer never emits, so it is an `accepted` spelling. The `json canonical` fence below is the writer's own output for the same distribution, on one line with the integer format version (distributions-0001). The YAML file stays canonical: it is the reference text form.

cases.title: The SDK dependency is keyed morphir/SDK
prose: Decision 0011. `morphir/sdk` is a valid name for some other package, so it is not rejected; it is simply not the SDK.

cases.title: Specs distribution
prose: A `Specs` distribution publishes a package's public face and nothing else: its member is `spec`, a package specification, where a `Library` carries `def`, a package definition. `packageName`, `dependencies` and `spec` are the three members the reader accepts; `dependencies` and `spec` may be omitted and default to empty, and a writer emits all three regardless (distributions-0002).
A `Specs` document has no `def`: an implementation is exactly what it does not carry.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Specs:
    packageName: example
    dependencies:
      morphir/SDK:
        modules: {}
    spec:
      modules:
        main:
          types: {}
          values:
            greet:
              inputs:
                name: morphir/SDK:string#string
              output: morphir/SDK:string#string

cases.title: Application distribution with entry points
prose: An `Application` is an executable package. It carries `packageName`, `dependencies`, `def` and `entryPoints`; `entryPoints` is required, because an application with no way in is not one. The dependency map holds package definitions rather than specifications, because an application links its dependencies statically. An entry point is keyed by a name the author chooses and holds `target`, `kind`, and an optional `doc`; the writer emits `doc` only when it is present, so `build` below has none.
`doc` belongs to an entry point, not to the distribution. An `Application` accepts exactly the four members above, so a `doc` beside them is an unknown member rather than package documentation.
`kind` is drawn from a fixed set: `main`, `command`, `handler`, `job`, `policy`.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Application:
    packageName: example
    dependencies: {}
    def:
      modules:
        main:
          Public:
            types: {}
            values:
              run:
                Public:
                  ExpressionBody:
                    inputTypes: {}
                    outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#unit
                    body:
                      Unit: {}
    entryPoints:
      start:
        target: example:main#run
        kind: main
        doc: The application entry point
      build:
        target: example:main#run
        kind: command

{ "formatVersion": 4, "distribution": { "Application": { "packageName": "example", "dependencies": {}, "def": { "modules": {} }, "entryPoints": {}, "doc": "Applications document their entry points, not themselves" } } }

cases.title: Later patch of a supported minor
prose: A patch of a supported minor is read; its canonical spelling stays the release string, since only the baseline collapses to the integer. Governed by `docs/spec/ir/format-version.md`, Revisions.

cases.title: A reserved $meta member belongs to document-tree files only
prose: `$meta` is reserved in the files of a document tree (document-tree-0005). A single document has no such member: at its root it is unknown.

cases.title: An application's dependencies are package definitions
prose: An `Application` links its dependencies statically (distributions-0007), so each entry of its `dependencies` is a package definition — access-controlled modules carrying definitions — where a `Library` or `Specs` entry is a package specification (distributions-0005, 0006).

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Application:
    packageName: example
    dependencies:
      my-org/shared:
        modules:
          util:
            Public:
              types: {}
              values:
                identity:
                  Public:
                    ExpressionBody:
                      inputTypes:
                        x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
                      outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
                      body:
                        Variable: x
    def:
      modules:
        main:
          Public:
            types: {}
            values:
              run:
                Public:
                  ExpressionBody:
                    inputTypes: {}
                    outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#unit
                    body:
                      Unit: {}
    entryPoints:
      start:
        target: example:main#run
        kind: main

cases.title: Manifest file
prose: The root file is `manifest`, never `format`. `pathBudget` is required per decision 0001.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 4000

formatVersion: 4
path: my-org/domain
types: [user, user-ID]
values: [get-user]

cases.title: Node filename is the escaped stem
prose: `user-ID` is stored as `user-_id.type.yaml`. Decision 0001.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 4000

formatVersion: 4
name: user-ID
def:
  Public:
    doc: The user's identifier
    TypeAliasDefinition:
      typeParams: []
      typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string

formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Library:
    packageName: my-org/my-project
    dependencies: {}
    def:
      modules:
        domain:
          Public:
            types:
              user-ID:
                Public:
                  doc: The user's identifier
                  TypeAliasDefinition:
                    typeParams: []
                    typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string
            values: {}

cases.title: A stem truncated for the path budget is recorded in fileNames
prose: Decision 0012. The budget is 64 characters from the distribution root. `pkg/my-org/my-project/domain/` is 29 characters and `.type.yaml` is 10, leaving 25 for the stem; a truncated stem keeps `25 - 10 = 15` characters of the escaped stem, drops any trailing `-` or `_`, and appends `__` plus the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the untruncated escaped stem. The module manifest maps the canonical name to the stem, and the name still appears under `types`.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 64

formatVersion: 4
path: domain
types: [customer-relationship-management-record]
values: []
fileNames:
  customer-relationship-management-record: customer-relati__44a101f8

formatVersion: 4
name: customer-relationship-management-record
def:
  Public:
    TypeAliasDefinition:
      typeParams: []
      typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string

formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Library:
    packageName: my-org/my-project
    dependencies: {}
    def:
      modules:
        domain:
          Public:
            types:
              customer-relationship-management-record:
                Public:
                  TypeAliasDefinition:
                    typeParams: []
                    typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string
            values: {}

cases.title: A top-level $meta member is reserved and ignored
prose: Decision 0014. A reader never reports `unknown_member` for `$meta` at the top level of a document-tree file, and never writes one. `session.jsonl` is daemon workspace state, not part of a distribution.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 4000
$meta:
  generator: example

formatVersion: 4
path: domain
types: []
values: []
$meta:
  generator: example

cases.title: The same tree in the JSON profile
prose: A `file` set is written in one profile, and a tree says the same thing in either. This is `document-tree-0003`'s set spelled in the JSON profile: the logical paths are identical — they carry no extension — and only the bytes of each document change, so a reader and a writer that agree on the tree must agree on both profiles.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Library:
    packageName: my-org/my-project
    dependencies: {}
    def:
      modules:
        domain:
          Public:
            types:
              user-ID:
                Public:
                  doc: The user's identifier
                  TypeAliasDefinition:
                    typeParams: []
                    typeExp: morphir/SDK:string#string
            values: {}

cases.title: A Private module
prose: A package definition's modules are access-controlled, so the module manifest carries an optional `access` member (document-tree page, "access (module manifest)"). It defaults to `Public` and a writer emits it only for a `Private` module, which keeps every existing manifest byte-identical while letting a private module round-trip through a tree.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 4000

formatVersion: 4
path: domain
access: Private
types: []
values: []

cases.title: A dependency lives under deps
prose: A tree holds its dependencies under `deps/<package path>/@<version>/`, laid out exactly as `pkg/` is below that segment. The segment beginning with `@` ends the package path, so a package named `a` and one named `a/b` can never claim the same directory; it is a bare `@` while the v4 model carries no package version (decision 0015). The distribution manifest lists each dependency package under `dependencies`, so discovery reads one file instead of walking `deps/`. A `Library` tree's dependencies are package specifications, so their node files carry `spec`.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Library
package: my-org/my-project
pathBudget: 4000
dependencies: [morphir/SDK]

formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Library:
    packageName: my-org/my-project
    dependencies:
      morphir/SDK:
        modules:
          basics:
            types:
              int:
                OpaqueTypeSpecification: {}
            values: {}
    def:
      modules:
        domain:
          Public:
            types: {}
            values: {}

cases.title: An application's dependencies are definitions under deps
prose: An `Application` links its dependencies statically (distributions-0010), so the node files under its `deps/` carry `def`, access-controlled like the package's own, where a `Library` or `Specs` tree's carry `spec` (document-tree-0008). The entry points live in the distribution manifest.

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution: Application
package: example
pathBudget: 4000
dependencies: [my-org/shared]
entryPoints:
  start:
    target: example:main#run
    kind: main

formatVersion: 4
name: identity
def:
  Public:
    ExpressionBody:
      inputTypes:
        x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
      outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
      body:
        Variable: x

formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Application:
    packageName: example
    dependencies:
      my-org/shared:
        modules:
          util:
            Public:
              types: {}
              values:
                identity:
                  Public:
                    ExpressionBody:
                      inputTypes:
                        x: morphir/SDK:basics#int
                      outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
                      body:
                        Variable: x
    def:
      modules:
        main:
          Public:
            types: {}
            values:
              run:
                Public:
                  ExpressionBody:
                    inputTypes: {}
                    outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#unit
                    body:
                      Unit: {}
    entryPoints:
      start:
        target: example:main#run
        kind: main

cases.title: Initialism as uppercase segment
prose: Decision 0001. A run of two or more single-letter legacy words decodes to one initialism.

cases.title: Single-letter type variable is a word
prose: Decision 0001, consequence 4. A run of one stays a word, so a type variable canonicalizes as `a`, never `(a)` or `A`.

cases.title: Retired parenthesized encoding is rejected
prose: Decision 0001 retired `value-in-(usd)`. GitHub #793 owns the books fixture that still carries it. A mixed-case segment such as Usd is also invalid: a segment is all lowercase or all uppercase, never mixed.

cases.title: The SDK package name
prose: Decision 0011: the SDK's canonical package name is `morphir/SDK`, because morphir-elm's `Path.fromString` splits `SDK` into single-letter words that decision 0001 decodes as one initialism. `morphir/sdk` is a different, valid name and is not rejected; distributions-0005 pins the dependency key.

cases.title: Legacy array items may be digits
prose: Decision 0012: both schemas use the core legacy word grammar `^[a-z0-9]+$`, so a digits-only word is legal. `["f", "r", "2052", "a"]` decodes as the naming corpus records: the letter run `f r` is one initialism, `2052` breaks the run, and the trailing `a` is a run of one, so a word.

cases.title: A digit word breaks an initialism run
Integer literal renamed
prose: `WholeNumberLiteral` is accepted on input and never written.

cases.title: Decimal literal keeps its text
prose: A decimal is carried as a string so no binding coerces it to a float.

cases.title: Document literal
prose: Decision 0013: the seventh literal carries a schema-less JSON-like tree verbatim, typed as `morphir/SDK:document#document`. Its payload is the document itself, so there is no `{ "value": .. }` spelling: `{ "DocumentLiteral": { "value": 1 } }` is the one-member document `{"value": 1}`. Number lexemes are preserved; a backend that reads `9007199254740993` through a 64-bit float fails this case visibly.

fences.body:
DocumentLiteral:
  name: Alice
  age: 30
  tags: [admin, user]
  metadata: null

cases.title: A document cannot be pattern matched
prose: Decision 0013: no `LiteralPattern` on a document.

cases.title: Nullary patterns
prose: Wildcard, empty-list and unit patterns take an empty payload, or `attributes` alone.

fences.body:
ConstructorPattern:
  fqname: morphir/SDK:maybe#just
  patterns:
    - AsPattern:
        pattern:
          WildcardPattern: {}
        name: x

HeadTailPattern:
  head:
    AsPattern:
      pattern:
        WildcardPattern: {}
      name: x
  tail:
    UnitPattern: {}

cases.title: Attributes are kept when compared with them

fences.body:
AsPattern:
  attributes:
    source:
      startLine: 2
      startColumn: 1
      endLine: 2
      endColumn: 2
  pattern:
    WildcardPattern: {}
  name: x

cases.title: Character literal
prose: A `CharLiteral` carries one character as a string, because JSON has no character type. One character means one code point, so an astral character is a single `CharLiteral` and a two-character string is not a character at all.

cases.title: A date-looking plain scalar is a string
prose: YAML 1.2 core has no implicit timestamps, and the YAML profile forbids implicit coercions, so a plain `2026-01-15` where a literal is expected is a `StringLiteral` and nothing else. YAML profile page, "Scalar resolution".

cases.title: Octal and hexadecimal integers are not accepted
prose: An IR integer literal carries its decimal lexeme. YAML 1.2 core resolves `0o17` and `0xF` to integers, but neither is a JSON lexeme, so the profile refuses them with `invalid_literal` and asks for decimal instead of inventing a spelling. YAML profile page, "Scalar resolution".

cases.title: A decimal literal is a decimal lexeme
prose: A `DecimalLiteral` is a genuine decimal, not text. Its payload is a string because JSON numbers are floats, but the string must spell a decimal: `[+-]?(digits(.digits?)?|.digits)([eE][+-]?digits)?`, no whitespace, no `_`, no hex, no `NaN` or `Infinity`. The lexeme is kept as written (patterns-and-literals-0002), so trailing zeros survive: `-0.00` is not `0`. Anything else is `invalid_literal`. v4 schema page, "Literals".

cases.title: A decimal lexeme may carry an exponent
prose: The grammar admits an exponent; the lexeme stays as written, so a reader does not expand `1e-7` to `0.0000001`. In YAML the lexeme is quoted, because a plain `1e-7` would resolve to a float.

cases.title: A decimal lexeme may omit the integer part
prose: `.5` is a decimal lexeme, and so is `12.`; neither is rewritten.

cases.title: An integer literal has arbitrary precision
prose: An `IntegerLiteral` carries a whole-number lexeme of any size; a binding that reads it through a 64-bit integer fails this case visibly. The lexeme is written back unchanged.

cases.title: A negative integer literal below the 64-bit range
Reference with one argument
prose: Closes bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.2 once the Rust decoder agrees.

cases.title: Record type
prose: Decision 0004: fields live under a `fields` member, so `attributes` can sit beside them. The field map directly under `Record`, which the schema documented until 2026-09-04, is accepted for the one-release window of decision 0006 and reported as `legacy_spelling`. The Rust encoder's `attrs` is the other window spelling a Record payload takes — it is a row of decision 0006's window table, not a decision of its own; this case pins it for type expressions and values-0013 pins it for values.

fences.body:
Record:
  fields:
    name: morphir/SDK:string#string
    age: morphir/SDK:basics#int

ExtensibleRecord:
  variable: r
  fields:
    email: morphir/SDK:string#string

cases.title: Function type
prose: Decision 0007: a Function type declares a `parameterType`. `argumentType` (the pre-decision schema) and `arg`/`result` (the Rust encoder) are accepted for the window of decision 0006. Bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.3.

cases.title: Attributes on type expressions
prose: Decision 0005: `attributes` is the optional first member of every expanded payload, and an empty one is never written. `attrs` is the Rust encoder's spelling, accepted for the window of decision 0006.

cases.title: Attributes are kept when compared with them
prose: A source location makes the expanded spelling the canonical one.

fences.body:
Variable:
  attributes:
    source:
      startLine: 1
      startColumn: 1
      endLine: 1
      endColumn: 2
  name: a

cases.title: Incompleteness is not a type expression
prose: Decision 0008 makes `Hole` a value expression (values-0009). The type-level incompleteness vocabulary — `Hole` with its reason, and `Draft` — is the v4 schema's `IncompleteTypeDefinitionBody`, which belongs to a definition, not to a type expression. A reader that meets either tag where a type belongs refuses it as an unknown node. The spellings themselves are pinned where they are read: definitions-0014 for a `Hole` with a `TypeMismatch` reason, definitions-0015 for `Draft`, and definitions-0016 for a `DeletedDuringRefactor` reason on an incomplete value definition.

cases.title: Attribute members are objects and nothing else is an attribute
prose: `constraints` and `extensions` are objects (v4 schema page, `TypeAttributes`); a member the schema does not name is unknown.

fences.body:
Apply:
  function:
    Reference: morphir/SDK:basics#negate
  argument:
    Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 1

cases.title: If-then-else member names
prose: Decision 0006: the schema's `then` and `else` are canonical; the Rust encoder's `thenBranch` and `elseBranch` are accepted for one release. Bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.3.

fences.body:
IfThenElse:
  condition:
    Literal:
      BoolLiteral: true
  then:
    Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 1
  else:
    Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 2

cases.title: Field access member names
prose: Decision 0006: `target` and `name`; the older `subject` and `fieldName` are accepted for one release.

fences.body:
Field:
  target:
    Variable: record
  name: field-name

cases.title: Tuple value
prose: Decision 0009: a Tuple always carries its wrapper; a bare array at value position is a List.

cases.title: Bare array and bare scalars at value position
prose: Decision 0009 closed bead morphir-ir-v4-stabilize.4: a bare array is a List, a bare number is an IntegerLiteral or FloatLiteral by its lexeme, and a bare boolean is a BoolLiteral. Writers keep the wrapped forms.

fences.body:
List:
  - Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 1
  - Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 2
  - Literal:
      IntegerLiteral: 3

cases.title: Hole
prose: Decision 0008: Hole stays a value expression with an optional `expectedType`; the Native and External expressions are removed, and a reader refuses them as unknown nodes. Native and external operations are definition bodies (definitions-0007).

cases.title: Bare scalars are literals
prose: Decision 0009. A bare `42` is an IntegerLiteral and a bare `true` a BoolLiteral; `4.0` is a FloatLiteral because its lexeme has a point. A bare string is never a StringLiteral (values-0002).

cases.title: Record value
prose: Decision 0004 applies to record values too; the direct field map is accepted for the window of decision 0006, and so is the Rust encoder's `attrs` spelling of `attributes`, a row of decision 0006's window table, which this case pins for values as types-0005 pins it for type expressions.

fences.body:
Record:
  fields:
    name:
      Variable: x
    age:
      Literal:
        IntegerLiteral: 25

Lambda:
  pattern:
    AsPattern:
      pattern:
        WildcardPattern: {}
      name: x
  body:
    Variable: x

cases.title: Let definition member names
prose: Decision 0006: `name`, `definition`, and `in`; the spec's older `valueName`, `valueDefinition`, and `inValue` are accepted for one release.

fences.body:
LetDefinition:
  name: x
  definition:
    ExpressionBody:
      inputTypes: {}
      outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
      body:
        Literal:
          IntegerLiteral: 1
  in:
    Variable: x

LetRecursion:
  definitions:
    f:
      ExpressionBody:
        inputTypes: {}
        outputType: morphir/SDK:basics#int
        body:
          Variable: f
  in:
    Variable: f

Destructure:
  pattern:
    TuplePattern:
      - AsPattern:
          pattern:
            WildcardPattern: {}
          name: a
      - WildcardPattern: {}
  value:
    Variable: pair
  in:
    Variable: a

PatternMatch:
  value:
    Variable: x
  cases:
    - pattern:
        LiteralPattern:
          IntegerLiteral: 0
      body:
        Literal:
          BoolLiteral: true
    - pattern:
        WildcardPattern: {}
      body:
        Literal:
          BoolLiteral: false

UpdateRecord:
  target:
    Variable: record
  fields:
    name:
      Literal:
        StringLiteral: new

cases.title: Attributes are kept when compared with them

fences.body:
Variable:
  attributes:
    source:
      startLine: 3
      startColumn: 5
      endLine: 3
      endColumn: 6
  name: x

cases.title: Reading a v3 literal into the model
prose: A v3 tagged array with capitalized tags decodes to the same value the v4 spelling does.

cases.title: Writing a Hole to v3 is refused
prose: The CLI refuses a v4 to v3 downgrade with `unsupported_v4_downgrade`. The kit grammar has no role for a write refusal yet; bead morphir-diwy specifies the rules for adding one. Until then this case is prose only.

cases.title: One YAML document
prose: The YAML profile admits exactly one document. A second document after `---`, or content after `...`, is refused rather than silently reading the first. YAML profile page, "Reader restrictions".

cases.title: No anchors, tags, merge keys or directives
prose: Anchors, aliases, explicit tags, merge keys, and directives are presentation and schema machinery the profile does not carry: an IR document means the same thing wherever it is read, so nothing in it may be resolved against something else. Each is refused with `unsupported_yaml_feature`. YAML profile page, "Reader restrictions".

fences.body:
formatVersion: 4
distribution:
  Library:
    packageName: example
    dependencies: &empty {}
    def:
      modules: *empty

cases.title: Duplicate keys
prose: A repeated mapping key is refused with `duplicate_member`, the same diagnostic the JSON profile reports for a repeated object member: last-one-wins would make the same bytes mean different things in different readers. YAML profile page, "Reader restrictions".

These are read and written at version 3 by any binding that declares version 3 (the Rust binding does; the reference declares only 4 and skips them). They pin the classic mirror against morphir-elm's codecs.

cases.title: A v3 decimal literal keeps its text
prose: morphir-elm encodes `DecimalLiteral` as a string (`Decimal.toString`); a binding that reads it through a float and writes `10.5` fails this case.

cases.title: A v3 derived type specification
prose: morphir-elm's fourth specification: `["DerivedTypeSpecification", params, { "baseType", "fromBaseType", "toBaseType" }]`, with the base type a v3 type and the two conversions v3 FQNames.

cases.title: v3 record fields are objects
prose: morphir-elm writes a record field as `{ "name", "tpe" }`, never as a pair.
